title: Batching SLO regression triage & hypothesis capture - May 6 2025
content:
Meeting: Quick triage (perf sync) - 2025-05-06 09:30 PT
Attendees: Maya Chen (owner), Arjun Patel, Kaitlin Reyes, Liam O'Connor, Sofia Martinez, Pedro (SRE on-call)
Location: #eng-serving-runtime -> perf-sync-standup
Goal: Capture hypotheses and short experiment plan to reproduce and isolate the p99 latency regression seen in canary after batchsize/autoscaling rollout.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Canary rollout of batching autoscaler change (auto-batchsize v2) correlated with p95/p99 tail increases on 2 GPU pools (eu-west-1 and us-west-2).
- End-to-end test runs show throughput drop ~18% and p99 increase +120ms for short requests (~32 token responses) under 95th percentile load profile.
- Suspected interaction between dynamic batchsize growth and prefix/KV cache behavior causing extra memcpy + extra attention kernel path for small sequences.
- Priority: repro reliably in lab, capture kernel traces, and rollback canary if impact confirmed on more canaries.

Observed signals and timeline:
- 2025-05-05 21:40 UTC: Canary deploy of auto-batchsize v2 (PR #4212) started (10% of traffic on dedicated pool a).
- 2025-05-05 22:10 UTC: Alerts: p99 latency up 40% on pool a. First page from SRE.
- 2025-05-05 22:30 UTC: Canary widened to 25% by rollout script (automation) - immediate increase persisted.
- 2025-05-05 23:10 UTC: Rollback initiated for canary (partial) but some traffic still routed due to stuck route.
- 2025-05-06 02:05 UTC: Engine team confirmed regression reproduced locally on nodes with mixed cache warmness.

Quick metrics snapshot (canary vs baseline):
- Baseline (stable 2025-05-04): p50=38ms, p95=84ms, p99=138ms, throughput=420 req/s
- Canary (auto-batch v2): p50=40ms, p95=105ms, p99=258ms, throughput=345 req/s 
- Sampled request types: short-gen (<=64 tokens) dominated regressions; long-gen (>512 tokens) unaffected.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Dynamic batchsize expansion increases intermediate KV cache churn for short sequences. When batch grows from small->larger during a request burst, we observe extra KV merges causing memcpy and extra CUDA kernel launches. This affects short responses particularly.
2) Kernel selector now chooses a different attention kernel for batch sizes >8 which regresses performance on certain GPU kernels (observed on A100-80GB mixed instances). Mismatch between heuristic and actual seq-len distribution.
3) Autoscaler interacts with runtime prefetching: aggressive batching defers flushes causing occasional head-of-line blocking and higher p99 due to long tail spikes.
4) Not related to batching code: coincident change in network stack (LB connection reuse) or tracer that increases serialization on path. Lower priority given current lab repro.

Repro plan (lab experiments) - short window runs (owner: Maya):
- Experiment matrix to run on perf-cpu/gpu lab pool (scale-run tool):
  * Variables: batch_limit = [4, 8, 12, 16], batch_growth_strategy = [static, auto-v1, auto-v2], kv_warmness = [cold, warm], seq_len = [32, 64, 128], model = rw-v1-small (FP16).
  * Traffic generator: rps profile shaped from production 95th percentile samples. 10m runs per cell.
- Logging: enable infra-kernel-tracing and cuda-profiler light mode for runs where p95/p99 diverge >20% from baseline. Collate nvprof timelines. (Arjun to help with trace config)
- Quick smoke: run batch_limit=8 static vs auto-v2 with seq_len=32, kv_warmness=warm to match canary sample. Reproduce in <60m. (target: today 2pm PT)

Quick results from local repro (collected tonight):
- Local run (seq_len=32, auto-v2): p95=110ms, p99=240ms, throughput down 15%. Trace slice shows extra kernel launch at t+3ms that performs KV gather+merge (approx 0.8ms extra).
- Kernel selection logs: observed switching from attention_kernel_X to attention_kernel_Y when batch > 8. Kernel_Y has worse measured latencies on 32-token sequences.
- Memory: no OOMs; small bump in device memory traffic (excess memcpy calls), not exceeding capacity.

Immediate mitigations suggested:
- Hotfix: revert auto-batchsize v2 and roll canary back to v1 until root cause confirmed (status: partial rollback in progress; Pedro coordinating).
- Short-term config: cap max_batch_size to 8 for pools using A100-80GB until kernel selector heuristics are adjusted. (Kaitlin to push config change)

Longer-term fixes and follow-ups:
- Improve kernel selector metrics: add sequence-length-aware microbenchmarks and embed a fast lookup table rather than heuristic. (owner: Arjun)
- Fix KV cache merge path to avoid extra memcpy for small batch merges: attempt zero-copy path or fuse merge op. (owner: Maya + infra kernel team)
- Add regression test in perf-ci: synthetic load with rapid batchsize oscillation to detect future regressions. (owner: Liam)
- Investigate whether prefetch/pipeline window interacts with batch growth. (owner: Sofia)

Open action items (owners + ETA):
- Maya: run experiment matrix and upload traces to /perf/traces/batchsize-may06 (ETA: 2025-05-06 EOD)
- Arjun: enable cuda light traces during smoke runs and extract kernel name switch events (ETA: 2025-05-07 noon)
- Kaitlin: push temporary config cap to 8 on pools eu-west-1/us-west-2 (ETA: 2025-05-06 afternoon)
- Pedro (SRE): complete canary rollback verification and confirm no route leakage (ETA: 2025-05-06 18:00 PT)
- Liam: draft perf-ci test and open PR to add to nightly synthetic suite (ETA: 2025-05-09)
- Sofia: reproduce in private cluster with mix of cold/warm KV cache and report differences (ETA: 2025-05-08)

Notes to self / meeting friction:
- Need better signal for kernel selection events in production logs; current logging at INFO is noisy. Propose compact telemetry for "kernel_switch" events with batch/seq_len tags.
- Concurrency: if we cap max_batch_size too low we may hurt throughput under steady high load; temporary cap must be coupled with monitoring alert to avoid regressions in throughput.
- Communicate clearly with product/customer-success if rollback affects SLA-backed Dedicated customers. (Customer-success loop: Kaitlin can coordinate draft message)

Attachments / commands used in lab runs (copied here):
- perf-run command (example): ./scale-run --model rw-v1-small --pool perf-gpu-a --rps-profile prod-95.json --duration 600 --batch-policy auto-v2 --max-batch 32 --trace cuda-light
- nvprof sample capture: nvprof --profile-from-start off --capture-range cudaProfApi -- output to nvprof-logs/run-<cell>.nvprof
- kernel log extraction: grep -E "attention_kernel|kv_merge|kernel_switch" app-logs/kernels.log | tail -n 200

Meeting decision bits:
- Immediate: apply config cap (max_batch_size=8) and complete rollback verification across canaries.
- Short-term (48-72h): complete lab repro + kernel traces and open PRs for hotfixes (kernel selector quick patch and cap enforcement).
- Medium-term (2-3 weeks): refactor KV merge path and add perf-ci tests.

If you have additional data (production traces, or perf-ci runs that look similar) paste them here or ping me directly. I'll update this doc as we confirm experiments.

Last updated: 2025-05-07 by Maya Chen
